status: experimental repository-local evidence; not CAWG conformance
question_mapping_status: Local provisional answers to Q5/Q6/Q9/Q10; Q1-Q23 crosswalk separately records open decisions. No CAWG adoption.

cases.name: Influencer sponsorship
cases.notes: New worked-case mapping: public sponsorship disclosure is distinct from consent to use a person's likeness.

question_mapping.Q5: Creator can use a recognized opaque subject; no routine legal identity resolution. AI performer representation remains open.
question_mapping.Q6: Brand and creator, publish, sponsored-post resource, advertising purpose, validity interval; does not grant likeness reuse.
question_mapping.Q9: Organization signature must be bound to a recognized brand signer with authority to commit that brand; local source authentication is not independent recognition.
question_mapping.Q10: Creator and sponsor roles are candidate public assertions; separately scoped co-signed grant/acceptance. CAWG decides endorsement relationship.

cases.specification_issue: CAWG use-case method refers to #286; case-specific normative issue assignment remains for Taskforce.
cases.policy_review: Session 6 identifies FTC Endorsement Guides and New York synthetic-performer disclosure if applicable. No legal applicability finding.

story.vision: A creator and platform want to substantiate a paid sponsorship claim without contacting the brand for every view.
story.actors: Brand, creator, platform, viewer; any person whose likeness is reused.
story.scope: A particular paid post. Likeness reuse in advertising and legal disclosure obligations are separate.
story.preconditions: Actual brand authority, signed sponsorship terms, creator acceptance, valid Content Credentials and appropriate status evidence.
story.success: Verify signed terms, subject/key and brand authority evidence independently; show a verified sponsorship only if the applicable public-claim policy is satisfied.
story.extensions: Missing deal, expired or revoked sponsorship: no verified label; absence is not proof of no sponsorship. Reuse of likeness: separate consent. Private agreement: pointer only.
story.frequency: Per relevant publication/use; no frequency estimate asserted.
story.special_requirements: No automatic private lookup; no inferred identity or consent; distinguish evidence from policy conclusion.

cases.name: Manager for a creator
cases.notes: Manager acceptance does not establish authority outside the signed terms.

question_mapping.Q5: Manager and creator have distinct opaque references and keys. No need to reveal personal identity to every viewer.
question_mapping.Q6: Publish post:1 for promotion in the stated interval; no inference of negotiation or onward delegation powers.
question_mapping.Q9: A company employing the manager does not automatically possess the creator's authority; separately establish delegation and corporate binding if used.
question_mapping.Q10: Candidate creator/manager role plus separate authority terms; endorsement alone cannot authorize publication.

cases.specification_issue: CAWG use-case method refers to #286; case-specific normative issue assignment remains for Taskforce.
cases.policy_review: Review disclosure/consent applicability by use; no specific legal rule assigned by the meeting.

story.vision: A manager wants to demonstrate authority to publish a creator's specified post, without acquiring the creator's identity or unlimited mandate.
story.scope: Specified publishing action for one promotional post, not general representation or transfer of authorship.
story.preconditions: Creator's recognized authority, manager key binding, both signatures, current status and bounded terms.
story.success: Check the manager's own countersignature and exact scope; independently evaluate recognition and authority.
story.extensions: Manager replaced, wrong post, expired grant, missing acceptance or new recipient: do not inherit prior permission.
story.frequency: Per relevant publication/use; no frequency estimate asserted.
story.special_requirements: No automatic private lookup; no inferred identity or consent; distinguish evidence from policy conclusion.

cases.name: Freelance reporter
cases.notes: Publishing authority does not establish the byline or legal authorship.

question_mapping.Q5: Reporter can be pseudonymous where publisher governance permits; binding and recognition remain necessary.
question_mapping.Q6: Publish article-1 for news within dates; not arbitrary articles or republishing rights.
question_mapping.Q9: Publisher organizational credential or key is insufficient without proof the signer may authorize this reporter.
question_mapping.Q10: Candidate creator role and publisher/endorsement semantics remain separate from scoped delegation; upstream decides representation.

cases.specification_issue: CAWG use-case method refers to #286; case-specific normative issue assignment remains for Taskforce.
cases.policy_review: Review applicable publication and subject-consent obligations; no legal conclusion from a valid byline.

story.vision: A freelance reporter wants a publisher and reader to distinguish publication authority from authorship.
story.actors: Publisher, reporter, editor or platform, reader.
story.scope: Publication of one article for news, not a general byline, editorial endorsement or copyright transfer.
story.preconditions: Recognized publisher, signer authorized to bind it, reporter acceptance, relevant signed manifest.
story.success: Verify publisher-to-reporter authority for the requested publication while preserving independent creative attribution.
story.extensions: Wrong article, substituted reporter, expired grant, byline dispute: no inferred authorship or authority.
story.frequency: Per relevant publication/use; no frequency estimate asserted.
story.special_requirements: No automatic private lookup; no inferred identity or consent; distinguish evidence from policy conclusion.

cases.name: Assistant on set
cases.notes: Creative-role attribution and subject consent remain separate.

question_mapping.Q5: Assistant and depicted subject are distinct references; no assumption that the delegate is the consent subject.
question_mapping.Q6: Transform photo-1 for editorial purpose in validity interval; no implied creation or unrelated use.
question_mapping.Q9: Studio signature requires authority to bind the production, not automatic rights over the depicted subject.
question_mapping.Q10: Candidate creative-role assertion must not substitute for the delegation; precise assertion and independent contribution signature remain open.

cases.specification_issue: CAWG use-case method refers to #286; case-specific normative issue assignment remains for Taskforce.
cases.policy_review: Review subject permission and minor/intimate-image safeguards as applicable; no legal determination.

story.vision: A production assistant wants the production team to verify permission for a specific transformation, without being treated as the author or subject-consent authority.
story.actors: Photographer, assistant, production platform, depicted subject.
story.scope: Transform photo-1 for editorial use; excludes creation, new purposes, or consent granted on behalf of depicted people.
story.preconditions: Recognized principal and assistant bindings, co-signed terms, any independently governed subject permission required.
story.success: Check allowed transformation, separate consent to use, and independent creative contribution if asserted.
story.extensions: Wrong action, changed photo, missing consent or minor subject: withhold unsupported conclusions; guardian authority is separate.
story.frequency: Per relevant publication/use; no frequency estimate asserted.
story.special_requirements: No automatic private lookup; no inferred identity or consent; distinguish evidence from policy conclusion.

cases.name: AI voice tool
cases.notes: Tool delegation does not establish voice-use consent or training permission.

question_mapping.Q5: Tool can be referenced by an opaque identifier; accountable principal and AI representation remain open under CAWG terminology.
question_mapping.Q6: Transform album-demos for demo within validity dates; training or unrelated album excluded.
question_mapping.Q9: A producer or tool company cannot confer performer consent solely by signing; verify organizational authority and subject consent separately.
question_mapping.Q10: Candidate identity/creative roles plus scoped tool authorization; no adopted AI or endorsement assertion representation.

cases.specification_issue: CAWG use-case method refers to #286; case-specific normative issue assignment remains for Taskforce.
cases.policy_review: Review the meeting's digital-replica/voice consent and synthetic-content disclosure group where applicable; no legal applicability finding.

story.vision: An artist wants a verifier to distinguish a voice tool's authorization to transform album demos from permission to use a person's voice.
story.actors: Artist or producer, voice tool/operator, performer, publisher.
story.scope: Transform specified album demos for demonstration, not training, general commercialization or voice ownership.
story.preconditions: Recognized principal, tool binding/representation, signed scope and independently governed voice-use consent as applicable.
story.success: Validate terms for the particular tool, resource, purpose and period; assess voice consent separately.
story.extensions: Wrong tool, album, purpose, expiry, withdrawn consent: independent non-positive outcomes; long-term rights/history require external evidence.
story.frequency: Per relevant publication/use; no frequency estimate asserted.
story.special_requirements: No automatic private lookup; no inferred identity or consent; distinguish evidence from policy conclusion.

cases.name: Pseudonymous creator
cases.notes: Self-declaration and key possession do not establish recognition or uniqueness.

question_mapping.Q5: Opaque subject can be a registry identifier, not a publicly resolvable personal identity; AI-reference semantics separately open.
question_mapping.Q6: Publish post:1 for promotion within dates; registry membership does not expand scope.
question_mapping.Q9: A guild or employer assertion cannot itself prove the principal granted the specific authority.
question_mapping.Q10: Candidate identity assertion with opaque subject plus distinct delegation; upstream determines representation and identity detail disclosure.

cases.specification_issue: CAWG use-case method refers to #286; case-specific normative issue assignment remains for Taskforce.
cases.policy_review: Review privacy, disclosure and consent obligations in context; do not treat pseudonymity as exemption.

story.vision: A creator wants a platform to evaluate permission without revealing legal identity or treating a pseudonym as proof of uniqueness.
story.actors: Creator, principal, industry registry, platform, viewer.
story.scope: Specific publication under a scoped opaque identity; no claim of uniqueness, universal identity or unbounded authority.
story.preconditions: Recognized source governance and pinned keys, opaque subject/key binding, valid delegation, relevant status evidence.
story.success: Use independently authenticated binding and authority evidence without private identity lookup; keep unresolved recognition visible.
story.extensions: Wrong key or subject, unrecognized source, stale or revoked evidence: no assured authority; role-restricted disclosure external.
story.frequency: Per relevant publication/use; no frequency estimate asserted.
story.special_requirements: No automatic private lookup; no inferred identity or consent; distinguish evidence from policy conclusion.
